checks: Concavity and maximality at zero give monotonicity on each side and endpoint limits at least their old positive values. Completion preserves concavity by taking limits in the chord inequalities. Endpoint changes affect planar and line integrals only on null sets. The completed compact superlevels are intervals and yield nonincreasing concave inverse arms continuous at both endpoints.

The line parameter (−q,sq) has arclength factor √(1+s²), canceled by coarea. The measure over levels at fixed w=|q| is the atom at w plus the integral of the derivative of v^(m−1). For m=1 the continuous part is absent. Its total equals R^(m−1)/2.

At fixed slope s>0 the atomic-layer equality A(w)=sw has at most one w. For the continuous layer, each v determines at most one w at equality. At s=0 a zero arm is possible only at the terminal level, which has zero joint mass. Thus the strict survival indicator reproduces the physical line measure despite possible conditional atoms.

Tonelli gives the volume and twice the t|q| moment, while vertical slicing at x=−w and x=w gives the gained positive side and lost negative side with kernel q(t−s)_+. Absolute integrability follows from the time moment.

The cited original formula used a maximum over superlevels without guaranteeing closure at its axial endpoints. The explicit endpoint repair precedes all uses here and preserves the section and volume data.

The joint survival and conditional atoms are additional records.
